kris.name: OI reversals vs revenue linkage
kris.risk: Order intake is de-booked (negative OBR) but the revenue already recognised is not adjusted, overstating revenue for the period.
kris.objective: Every OI reversal has a matching revenue treatment; the OI → revenue linkage holds on CPO number.
steps: Extract all OI bookings and reversals for the period from the Order Booking System (full population, no sampling).
Match each reversal to the original booking on CPO number and WBS.
Pull revenue postings for the same CPO / WBS from SAP and the Management Reporting revenue view.
Where a reversal exists, check that revenue was reversed, re-booked, or never recognised.
Search the Order Booking System for a re-booking of the same CPO on another WBS within the re-booking window.
Classify each item as explainable (re-booked, timing, correction) or unexplained, with the reasoning shown.

thresholds.label: Planner trigger: unexplained items per region

kris.name: Order intake accuracy (CPO ↔ SAP ↔ OBS)
kris.risk: OI is booked in the wrong period, for the wrong amount, or without a valid customer PO.
kris.objective: OI is booked correctly, in the correct period, for the correct amount.
steps: Extract the OI (YCA) report from SAP for the period: WBS, project, currency, amount, booking text.
Extract the Order Booking System list with CPO reference, PO date, PO value and accepting manager.
Reconcile every line three ways: customer PO → SAP → Order Booking System (period, amount, currency, description, discounts).
Flag OI booked higher than PO value with no correction in the quarter.
Flag bookings where the PO date is after the booking date (cut-off).
Populate the testing template for the whole population and hand exceptions to the reviewer.

thresholds.label: Planner trigger: unexplained items per region

kris.name: Period-end de-booking clustering
kris.risk: Corrections and de-bookings cluster in the final days of a period, indicating OI managed to a target rather than to the customer PO.
kris.objective: De-bookings are spread through the period and each has a documented business reason.
steps: Extract all negative OI lines (corrections, de-bookings) for the period from the Order Booking System.
Bucket by days-before-close and by WBS, region and business group (BG-A / BG-B).
Flag any WBS or region where de-bookings in the last N days exceed the threshold share.
For flagged clusters, read the booking text for a stated reason and check for a re-booking in the next period.

thresholds.label: Share of period de-bookings in window

kris.name: Order backlog completeness
kris.risk: Backlog reported to management does not reconcile to booked OI less recognised revenue.
kris.objective: OBL = cumulative OI − cumulative revenue for every open WBS.
steps: Recompute backlog per WBS from SAP OI and revenue postings.
Compare with the Management Reporting backlog view for the same period.
Flag WBSs where the difference exceeds tolerance and trace to the causing posting.

thresholds.label: Planner trigger: unexplained items per region

kris.name: WBS – project – currency consistency
kris.risk: OI is booked on a WBS whose project, customer or currency does not match the CPO.
kris.objective: Every OI line sits on a WBS that belongs to the CPO customer and currency.
steps: Pull WBS master (project, customer, currency) from Project Master.
Join OI lines to WBS master and compare customer and currency with the CPO.
Flag mismatches and WBSs closed before the booking date.

thresholds.label: Planner trigger: unexplained items per region

kris.name: Duplicate payments – assurance over business monitoring
kris.risk: The CCM duplicate-check run by the S2P team misses true duplicates or is not operating as designed.
kris.objective: IA validates the business control rather than re-performing it; re-test a sample of its flagged and cleared items.
steps: Ingest the CCM duplicate-check output for the period (flagged vs cleared).
Re-perform the duplicate test on a risk-weighted sample of cleared items.
Report on control effectiveness, not on individual invoices.

exceptions.summary: OI of EUR 860,000 was de-booked on 27 Aug (one day before close). Revenue of EUR 215,000 recognised in P7 on this CPO was not reversed and no re-booking was found.

evidence.value: OI +860,000 EUR, WBS N.10871.03, accepted by manager AM-104
OI −860,000 EUR (negative OBR), text: "cust scope change"
No booking for CPO 4500120011 on any WBS

reasoning: Step 2 matched reversal 90577 to booking 88213 on CPO number and WBS.
Step 4 found revenue already recognised in P7 (EUR 215,000) with no adjustment in P8 – the OI → revenue linkage is broken.
Step 5 searched 30 days (threshold) for a re-booking and found none, so the "re-booked on a new WBS" explanation does not apply.
The booking text says "cust scope change" but there is no revised CPO attached; a scope change would normally leave a reduced OI, not zero.

hypothesis.text: Revenue adjustment missed after de-booking. Most likely a missed handover between market operations (who reversed the OI) and project finance (who own the revenue posting).

exceptions.confirm: Ask project finance for the revised CPO or the revenue reversal reference for P9. If a revised CPO exists, expect a re-booking at the reduced value.

exceptions.summary: OI of EUR 1,240,000 was de-booked on 28 Aug and re-booked for the same amount on WBS N.10234.02 on 2 Sep. Revenue linkage moves with the new WBS.

evidence.value: OI −1,240,000 EUR, text: "WBS split – move to .02"
OI +1,240,000 EUR, WBS N.10234.02, same CPO
Created 26 Aug 2026 under the same project
No revenue recognised yet on this CPO

reasoning: Step 5 found a re-booking of the identical CPO and amount inside the 30-day window.
Project Master confirms the target WBS belongs to the same project, so this is a structural move, not a lost order.
No revenue had been recognised, so nothing needed adjusting.
Flagged only because the reversal crossed a period boundary – the pattern is explainable and consistent with the booking text.

hypothesis.text: Project split into two WBSs; OI moved rather than lost. No revenue impact.

exceptions.confirm: Nothing further required. Consider a rule to auto-clear reversals that are re-booked on the same CPO within the window.

exceptions.summary: Partial de-booking of EUR 430,000 out of EUR 1,900,000 on 29 Aug. Revenue of EUR 610,000 already recognised is higher than the remaining OI would support at the project margin.

evidence.value: Backlog reduced by 430,000 – consistent with reversal

reasoning: Reversal text states a discount, which is a legitimate reason for a partial de-booking.
However revenue already recognised was computed on the original OI; a 22.6% price reduction should trigger a revenue true-up.
No true-up posting was found in P8; the backlog view moved but the revenue view did not.

hypothesis.text: Discount applied to OI but not pushed through to revenue recognition – possible timing (true-up may land in P9).

exceptions.confirm: Re-check after P9 close. If no true-up appears, raise with project finance.

exceptions.summary: De-booking on 30 Aug corrects a duplicate booking made on 29 Aug for the same CPO. Net OI is unchanged.
reasoning: Two identical bookings within one minute followed by a reversal of one – a classic duplicate correction.
Net position matches the CPO value.

hypothesis.text: Duplicate entry corrected same period. No impact.

exceptions.summary: 6 of the 9 de-bookings on this project in P8 (67%) fell in the last 3 days before close, totalling EUR 1.62m. Threshold is 40%.

evidence.value: No revenue adjustments on the project

reasoning: Share of de-bookings in the period-end window (67%) is above the 40% threshold.
Two lines carry no business reason at all.
The same project appears in OI-02 exception X-1041 – two independent KRIs point at the same WBS family.

hypothesis.text: OI on this project is being adjusted at period end to manage the reported figure rather than to reflect customer POs.

exceptions.confirm: Candidate for a pointed spot audit (1–2 weeks) on Customer A OI. Sent to the Planner as a residual-risk trigger.

exceptions.summary: 2 of 2 de-bookings fell on 29 Aug; both re-booked in P9 on a corrected currency (GBP).
reasoning: Small population (2 lines) trips the share threshold trivially.
Both re-booked next period in the correct currency – a mechanical correction.

hypothesis.text: Currency correction across a period boundary. No risk.

exceptions.confirm: Consider a minimum-population guard of 4 lines on this threshold.

exceptions.summary: OI booked at EUR 2,100,000 against a customer PO of EUR 1,950,000 (+7.7%). No correction in the quarter.

evidence.value: PO value 1,950,000 EUR, PO date 11 Apr 2026

reasoning: Variance of 7.7% is above the 1% tolerance.
No PO amendment attached in Order Booking System; no correction in the quarter.

hypothesis.text: Booking included an expected change order that was never confirmed by the customer.

exceptions.confirm: Confirmed as an observation by reviewer on 15 Jul; raised with the account manager.

exceptions.summary: OI booked 28 Jun; customer PO dated 2 Jul. Signed LOI on file dated 25 Jun.
reasoning: PO date after booking date trips the cut-off test.
Policy v4.1 §3.2 allows booking on a signed LOI where the PO follows within 10 working days – it did.

hypothesis.text: Permitted LOI-based booking. No exception under policy v4.1.

exceptions.confirm: Accepted. Rule updated to recognise LOI attachments.

exceptions.summary: CPO in USD; OI booked in EUR at 0.921 vs the month table rate of 0.915 (0.6% variance).
reasoning: Variance is within the 1% tolerance once the rate difference is isolated.
Rate used matches the daily rate on the booking date, not the month table.

hypothesis.text: Daily vs monthly rate. Within tolerance.
